## Design

### 2026-10-09 – October 9th, 2026: Parts and PCB

**7h**

October 9th, 2026: Parts and PCB

I started looking for all of the parts for my PCB from LCSC so I could use them in EasyEDA.

The easy parts I found:
- 6x6 tactile push buttons*
- Piezo buzzer
- The screen/pin header
- Joystick Module*
- 12x12 tactile push buttons
*I ended up using 6 12x12 buttons because the 6x6 were small and the joystick was too big.*
I was debating whether to put the screen directly on the PCB or use a pin header, but I eventually decided on a pin header because it would be easier to test and replace.

![PCB Model V1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/894c928767b5607b7fd6a40c01de4b20da77a373f642d89bbe792831b8536e14.png)

I really spent a lot of time trying to get the Xiao RP2040 Plus footprint.

![Xiao RP2040 PCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/b2ec11e85e815f66f648ed5623d57417f42209f4023e9c8bad87a0ad7a2d052e.png)

Issues:
- I could not find the RP2040 Plus in EasyEDA
I found it on the Seeed Studio Website https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO-RP2040/#xiao-rp2040-plus
- I ended  up trying to model the RP2040 Plus myself with the proper spacing
I ended up getting confused between spec sheets, and I'm fairly new to EasyEDA, so it was too difficult for me to understand.
- Seeed's Eagle export is the same as the KiCad export
I found the button to import KiCad models, and after some "extensive" research, I found out that KiCad models are mostly compatible with EasyEDA. For some reason, the pads had x's over them, but I chose to ignore that for now.
![PCB Layout V2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/b2b7759676c39f7fe945572ce996f41e236f6f897cb30dc4341c694723a6a8b5.png)

After all that, I thought I had the full footprint, but it was missing the bottom pads.... I was able to figure out how to place the pads on the footprint, and I used the PCB from the KiCad import to measure the pad positions. I can use this to make custom footprints if it was this easy.
 ![Custom Xiao Footprint](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/af87eeaee903b82a713252dc8c5954f20d3c14f5904b5505393c4d39515d3db2.png)

Now I just made sure everything actually fit on the board and made sure the silkscreen was ok, setting myself up to route the PCB next.
![PCB Board V3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/def0a4262a7ad10bebc948ec8fe3eb281f36b158366536699d7e03c5a8a6b421.png)
I took one look over the PCB and actually finished it. I added the 8-pin header for the Gyro/Accelerometer (MPU-9250), the battery charging pads on the RP2040, the holes for the 2-Pin JST battery connector, and an on/off switch.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/488a10680c394661c4fdcad5bbd8905acb0a0b7a20eb597bc5b96435eb74f9da.png)
Did a little more research and added a switch and some leds for power and progrmming LED. This is the actual final PCB and all i have to do is just route it.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/0dc790a0a64bf460990ab85a916247922026f6bf8452864e500f3aa8caa838dc.png)
